reason: The transporter-bearing cell appears ready to take in the glucose needed for energy production.
expectation: The cell will take in fuel for the steps that produce ATP.

alternatives.reason: The mitochondria also appear relevant to turning fuel into usable energy.

effect: The transporter-bearing cell combined with the fibre structures, so I now have a muscle fibre scaffold to equip.
reaction: I was surprised that the fuel combination instead led to assembling the fibre.
reason: The thin and thick filaments appear to be the complementary parts of the fibre's contractile machinery.
expectation: They will form a contractile unit that can be added to the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed sliding filament units, which appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre scaffold.
reaction: The overlapping arrangement makes their relationship clearer.
reason: The scaffold has spaces for contractile units, so these units appear to belong in it.
expectation: The sliding filament units will become part of the muscle fibre.

effect: The sliding filament units are now installed in the muscle fibre. It still appears to need usable energy and signals to pull and relax.
reaction: Filling the fibre with the overlapping units was a clear assembly step.
reason: Mitochondria use glucose and oxygen in energy production, so this pair seems relevant to making ATP.
expectation: The mitochondria will use the fuel and oxygen in a step toward producing ATP.

effect: The fuel and oxygen produced fuelled mitochondria; the picture shows glucose being split in the cell fluid before smaller molecules enter the mitochondrion.
reaction: The distinction between the cell fluid and mitochondrion made the energy sequence clearer.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the remaining ingredients for making ATP, and the fuelled mitochondria appear ready to supply the energy.
expectation: The mitochondria will produce ATP from ADP and phosphate.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply, with the picture showing ATP going to the pulling machinery and its components returning.
reaction: The cycle makes the continuing energy supply clearer.
reason: The filament-filled fibre needs ATP for its pulling machinery.
expectation: The ATP supply will equip the fibre to pull.

effect: The fibre is now ATP-ready; the covered binding site suggests it still needs a signal before pulling.
reaction: The picture clarified that ATP helps the myosin head release and reset.
reason: The calcium signal appears to be the next step in activating the fibre's filaments.
expectation: Calcium will allow the filaments to interact and the fibre to pull.

effect: The calcium signal exposed grip sites, allowing the filaments to slide and the fibre to shorten. The fibre still needs to relax.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments sliding was clear.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes appear able to remove calcium from around the filaments so the fibre can relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the muscle fibre to relax.

effect: The calcium pumps returned calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping pulling. An outside pull then relaxed the fibre, completing the goal.
reaction: I found it useful that relaxation also requires ATP.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium signal and shortening fibre were most worthwhile: the description connected the signal to exposed grip sites and made clear that the filaments slide rather than shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the sliding filament units was a clear but predictable assembly step; it added less explanation than the later pulling sequence.

surprise.text: I had expected ATP simply to power pulling, so seeing it help myosin release and reset, and then power calcium pumping during relaxation, broadened my understanding.

arbitrary.text: My first attempt to give the transporter-bearing cell glucose and oxygen seemed plausible from the titles, but the compatibility feedback redirected it to fibre assembly. The purpose became clear once I saw the result.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the sequence made the connection between cellular energy and muscle movement concrete, and I am curious how the fibre will connect to larger body systems.
